newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields continued their fall on Tuesday in foreign-driven trade.

Six-month T-bill rates were unchanged at 4.73 percent and the nine year bond yields dropped two basis points to 7.35 percent, a year low. The spread between Swedish and German long yields decreased one basis point to 126, also a year low.
The undertone in the market was still very strong, but to a certain extent dealers were sidelined ahead of U.S. jobless data due on Friday.
Dealers were now concerned about how long the downward trend would hold.
"There has been some surprising buying. At the same time foreigners have sold off, so the strength is a bit unexpected," one dealer said.
"Many actors are playing a waiting game and it's mainly some major buyers that have been active in the market," another said.
Yields could fall more ahead of the National Debt Office's auction of three billion crowns worth of four year bonds on Wednesday, another dealer said.
The crown was stable at 4.3400 against the mark compared to 4.3385 late on Monday.
